findings.passage: “The findings underscore the need for voter identification on a national level, and we should begin by strengthening these measures right here at home.”
findings.note: Quoted in a House caucus release on double voting between Ohio and Pennsylvania; says voter identification should be strengthened, nationally and in the state.

findings.passage: “This report involves millions of voting records, and analyzing this data takes time to ensure accuracy. From where we stand today, we can confirm that double voting occurred in previous national elections, but we are committed to thoroughly finalizing this report,” said Flick.
findings.note: Same release; his description of his voter-record comparison between two states.

findings.passage: In addition, I support proposed legislation to strengthen voter ID, reduce the size of our state government, reduce property taxes for veterans and senior citizens and create Supreme Court term limits.
findings.note: Part of a first-year statement on his site; says he supports proposed legislation to strengthen voter ID. No bill number named.

findings.passage: “I oppose the governor’s mandate to automatically register residents to vote when they renew their driver’s licenses or ID cards at PennDOT driver and photo license centers. Why? Three reasons.
findings.note: His statement against automatic voter registration at PennDOT; does not address ID to vote.
